description: Shared producer rules for turning client URL expressions and declared HTTP wrapper calls into route-call templates: interpolation, query tails, base joins, stripping, masking, and wrapper argument binding.

cases.note: Only an interpolation that fills a whole segment becomes {}. Partial call segments are dynamic even though server templates may use p{}s.
A value before the first literal slash is a base expression; apply compose.base-join instead of this rule.
A trailing local whose initializer provably starts with '?' or is empty/orEmpty on every other branch is a query tail.
DefaultUriBuilderFactory copies the base builder and appends the template path as a plain string (FullPathComponentBuilder.append).
The concatenation is /api//users; getSanitizedPath collapses every // in the path (not only after the scheme).
No slash is inserted between the base path and a relative template.
With no base path the URI string inserts / after the authority, so the relative template is not glued to the host (unlike dio). Confirmed by the kartograph Spring client oracle.
DefaultUriBuilderFactory never calls normalize(); the kartograph oracle recorded the request path with the dot segments intact.
Unknown base: a rooted template is a base-anchored suffix; // collapses in the template too.
Without the base path the plain concatenation cannot be resolved (like dio).
RestTemplateBuilder.rootUri prepends the root only to templates starting with /; the result is parsed without a base (// collapses).
A template not starting with / gets no root and has no host, so no request path can be claimed.
HttpServiceMethod.initUrl inserts / only when the type url does not end with / and the method url does not start with /; the result then joins the client base like spring-uri-builder.
A present but non-literal argument is methodDynamic; the default applies only when the argument is omitted.
Only the exact upper-case verb literal is a verb; map other spellings through methodEnum.
(*url.URL).ResolveReference merges a relative reference after the last / of the base path (RFC 3986 5.2.3). Reproduced with go1.27.1; go1.23.0 source is identical.
Without a trailing slash the last base segment is replaced, not extended.
An absolute-path reference replaces the whole base path.
remove_dot_segments (RFC 3986 5.2.4) runs after the merge.
A network-path reference (//host/...) replaces the authority as well as the path.
(*url.URL).JoinPath (Go 1.19+) joins with path.Join, so the base path is always extended.
A leading / on an element does not reset the path (unlike ResolveReference).
path.Join collapses repeated slashes.
path.Join cleans .. against the base path, so it can leave the base path.
JoinPath keeps one trailing slash when the last element ends with /.
Unknown base: the cleaned element path is a tail behind the unknown base path.
Unknown base: which segment .. removes cannot be known.
SetBaseURL trims trailing slashes and parseRequestURL prefixes a missing / before concatenating (resty v2.17.2; v3.0.0-rc.4 composes the same path). Recorded as the RequestURI seen by a local server.
A leading / does not reset the base path (plain concatenation, not RFC 3986).
The concatenation is sent as is; // is not collapsed.
Dot segments are not removed; the server receives /api/./users.
Unlike rfc3986 a rooted path stays behind the unknown base.

url::Url::join parses the input with the base (WHATWG URL Standard); for these http(s) inputs the result equals RFC 3986 resolution. reqwest has no base URL, so this applies only when the code calls Url::join. Reproduced with url 2.5.8.
Url::join docs: without a trailing slash the last path component is a file name and is replaced.
./ is removed; the rest is a tail behind the unknown base directory.
Unknown base: which segment .. removes cannot be known.
The base_url setter enforces a trailing / and _merge_url appends the relative path (httpx 0.28.1).
_merge_url strips every leading / of the relative path, so a rooted path does not reset the base path (unlike RFC 3986).
normalize_path (RFC 3986 5.2.4) runs on the merged URL, so .. can leave the base path.
URL('//users') parses users as a host with an empty path; the request goes to the base path. Producers do not claim a route for it.

ClientSession._build_url joins with yarl URL.join (RFC 3986). Base URLs with a path and relative paths without a leading / are accepted since aiohttp 3.11. Reproduced with aiohttp 3.14.3 / yarl 1.25.1.
As in RFC 3986 a rooted path replaces the base path (aiohttp docs: request URLs should have no leading slash).
The origin-only form accepted since aiohttp 3.8.
ClientSession raises ValueError('base_url must have a trailing /'); no request is made.
A rooted path works on every base_url form since aiohttp 3.8 (origin-only base in 3.8-3.10, a base path is replaced from 3.11).
Relative paths without a leading / are accepted since aiohttp 3.11; a producer that cannot prove 3.11+ emits dynamic + ambiguous-base-join:.
